title: What the Query Remembers: Query Abstraction Governs Lexical and Dense Retrieval of Classical Arabic Poetry
abstract: arXiv:2610.31821v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: How well a poetry archive can be searched depends on what the user still remembers, not only on what the model understands. We show this for Classical Arabic poetry, benchmarking nine dense encoders and BM25 over two corpora, three indexing modes and two evaluation protocols. Which retriever wins is governed by how much of a poem's wording the query still carries. On tip-of-the-tongue queries BM25 leads every dense encoder, including an 8B state-of-the-art model (0.746 vs. 0.717 Recall@5); on abstract queries it falls to eighth out of ten (0.392 vs. 0.748). Editing the wording of the same queries shows that this ranking largely reflects query composition: adding one remembered half-verse raises BM25 by 38 points, rewriting the quoted words by hand leaves BM25 level with the 8B encoder, and BM25's sensitivity to remembered wording is significantly steeper than that of the strongest dense encoder. translated_title: 查询所记住的：查询抽象程度决定古典阿拉伯语诗歌的词汇检索与稠密检索
translated_abstract: 一个诗歌档案库能被搜索得多好，取决于用户还记得什么，而不仅仅是模型理解了什么。我们在古典阿拉伯语诗歌上验证了这一点，在两个语料库、三种索引模式和两种评估协议下，对九个稠密编码器和BM25进行了基准测试。哪个检索器胜出，取决于查询中仍然保留了多少诗歌原文的措辞。在“话到嘴边”（tip-of-the-tongue）型查询上，BM25领先所有稠密编码器，包括一个8B参数的最先进模型（Recall@5为0.746对0.717）；而在抽象查询上，BM25则跌至十个系统中的第八位（0.392对0.748）。对相同查询措辞的编辑实验表明，这种排名很大程度上反映了查询的构成：添加一句被记住的半行诗可使BM25提升38分；手工改写引用的词语后，BM25与8B编码器持平；而且BM25对被记住措辞的敏感度显著高于最强的稠密编码器。同样的维度也支配着解释增强方法。
tldr: 该论文发现，在古典阿拉伯语诗歌检索中，查询保留诗歌原文措辞的程度（即查询的抽象程度）决定了检索器的优劣——记忆型查询下BM25领先所有稠密模型，而抽象查询下稠密编码器胜出，且BM25对措辞变化的敏感度远高于稠密模型。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that in Classical Arabic poetry retrieval, query abstraction—how much of a poem's wording the query still retains—governs which retriever wins, with BM25 leading on tip-of-the-tongue queries but falling behind dense encoders on abstract queries, and BM25 being far more sensitive to remembered wording than the strongest dense model.
